question: Which of the following is NOT a part of service sector in India? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 1)
options: Banking
Transport
Agriculture
Insurance
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agriculture

Explanation:
The Indian economy is divided into three major sectors: primary, secondary, and tertiary. The service sector (tertiary sector) includes all activities that provide services rather than producing goods, such as banking, transport, insurance, education, healthcare, tourism, etc. Agriculture is part of the primary sector because it involves the extraction of natural resources to produce goods. The service sector contributes the largest share to India's GDP and is considered the backbone of the country's economy. Therefore, among the given options, only agriculture is not a part of the service sector.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Contribution of service sector to India's GDP → Approximately 55%
☛ Primary sector includes → Agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining
☛ Secondary sector includes → Manufacturing, construction, electricity
☛ Tertiary sector includes → Banking, insurance, transport, communication, tourism
☛ Largest sub-sector of service sector → Financial and business services
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भारत में सेवा क्षेत्र का हिस्सा नहीं है? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: बैंकिंग
परिवहन
कृषि
बीमा
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है कृषि

Explanation:
भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था को तीन प्रमुख क्षेत्रों में बांटा गया है: प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक और तृतीयक। सेवा क्षेत्र (तृतीयक क्षेत्र) में वे सभी गतिविधियाँ शामिल हैं जो उत्पादन के बजाय सेवाएँ प्रदान करती हैं, जैसे बैंकिंग, परिवहन, बीमा, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, पर्यटन आदि। कृषि प्राथमिक क्षेत्र का हिस्सा है, क्योंकि इसमें प्राकृतिक संसाधनों का दोहन करके वस्तुओं का उत्पादन किया जाता है। सेवा क्षेत्र भारत के GDP में सबसे बड़ा योगदान देता है और यह देश की अर्थव्यवस्था की रीढ़ है। इसलिए, दिए गए विकल्पों में से केवल कृषि सेवा क्षेत्र का हिस्सा नहीं है।

question: First Five Year Plan in India was from- (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: 1951 - 1956
1950 - 1955
1947 - 1952
1949 - 1954
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1951 - 1956

Explanation:
The first Five Year Plan in India was implemented from 1951 to 1956. This plan focused primarily on agriculture and irrigation as the country was facing food grain shortages. It was based on the Harrod-Domar model and aimed for an annual growth rate of 2.1%, which actually achieved 3.6%. The plan period was from April 1951 to March 1956. The first Five Year Plan was considered successful and laid the foundation for self-sufficiency in food grains. It was launched under the prime ministership of Jawaharlal Nehru.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ First Five Year Plan duration → 1951-1956
☛ Primary focus of First Five Year Plan → Agriculture and irrigation
☛ Model of First Five Year Plan → Harrod-Domar model
☛ Target growth rate of First Five Year Plan → 2.1%
☛ Prime Minister during First Five Year Plan → Jawaharlal Nehru
question_hi: भारत में पहली पंचवर्षीय योजना _________ से थी। (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (30/03/2019) Shift 3)
options_hi: 1951 - 1956

Explanation:
भारत में पहली पंचवर्षीय योजना 1951 से 1956 तक लागू की गई थी। इस योजना का मुख्य फोकस कृषि और सिंचाई क्षेत्रों पर था, क्योंकि उस समय देश खाद्यान्न की कमी से जूझ रहा था। यह योजना हैरोड-डोमर मॉडल पर आधारित थी और इसका लक्ष्य 2.1% की वार्षिक वृद्धि दर प्राप्त करना था, जो वास्तव में 3.6% रही। योजना की अवधि अप्रैल 1951 से मार्च 1956 तक थी। पहली पंचवर्षीय योजना को सफल माना गया और इसने देश को खाद्यान्न में आत्मनिर्भर बनने की दिशा में अग्रसर किया। यह योजना जवाहरलाल नेहरू के प्रधानमंत्रित्व काल में शुरू की गई थी।

question: The merger of Railway and Union budget came into effect from (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: 2017-2018
2016-2017
2004-2005
2000-2001
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2017-2018

Explanation:
The merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget came into effect from the financial year 2017-2018. Before this merger, the Railway Budget was presented separately since 1924. The decision was announced by Finance Minister Arun Jaitley in his 2016 budget speech to end the practice of a separate 'surcharge budget' and bring more transparency to railway finances. This merger integrated railway plans directly into the central budget, making resource allocation more efficient and aligned with overall national priorities.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When did the merger of Railway and Union Budget take effect? → 2017-2018
☛ Since when was the Railway Budget presented separately before merger? → 1924 (for about 93 years)
☛ Who announced the merger of Railway Budget? → Finance Minister Arun Jaitley (in 2016)
☛ What was the main objective of the merger? → To end the practice of a separate 'surcharge budget'
☛ After merger, railway plans became part of which budget? → Central/Union Budget

question: Which of the following industries generates invisible exports? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Automobile
Food
Tourism
Crude oil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tourism

Explanation:
Invisible exports are services that earn foreign exchange without involving tangible goods. The tourism industry generates income by providing services such as accommodation, transport, and guidance to tourists, which are not physical goods. Automobile, food, and crude oil are tangible goods, and their export is considered visible export. In India, tourism is a major source of service exports and plays a vital role in earning foreign currency.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Example of invisible exports → Tourism, banking, insurance, software services
☛ Example of visible exports → Automobiles, crude oil, food grains
☛ Largest service export sector in India → Software and IT services
☛ India's rank in tourism exports → 10th globally (2019)
☛ Balance of invisible trade → Measured by difference between exports and imports of services
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उद्योग अदृश्य निर्यात सृजित करता है? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: What is the situation called in the foreign exchange market when the value of the domestic currency starts falling in comparison to the foreign currency? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: devaluation
cost overrun
revaluation
liquidation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is devaluation

Explanation:
In the foreign exchange market, when the value of the domestic currency starts falling in comparison to foreign currency, it is called devaluation. This situation is typically done deliberately by the government or central bank to boost exports and make imports expensive. Devaluation reduces the purchasing power of the currency and can affect foreign investment. It occurs under a fixed exchange rate system, while depreciation is caused by market forces.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Under which exchange rate system does devaluation occur? → Fixed exchange rate system
☛ What is the main objective of devaluation? → To boost exports
☛ What is the opposite process of devaluation called? → Revaluation
☛ What is the fall in currency value due to market forces called? → Depreciation
☛ Which sector benefits from devaluation? → Export sector

question: If the government starts purchasing its bonds before their maturity period (on the full maturity amount), in this situation what will the money circulating in the economy be called? (RPF SI 2018 (24/12/2018) Shift 1)
options: Heated Currency
cheap currency
easy currency
Expensive currency
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cheap currency

Explanation:
When the government purchases its bonds before maturity, it injects additional liquidity into the economy. This increases the money supply and lowers interest rates, making money cheaper. This process is known as monetary expansion. Cheap currency means borrowing becomes easier and cheaper, stimulating investment and economic activity. In contrast, expensive currency occurs when the central bank sells bonds to reduce money supply, raising interest rates. This action is taken by the government to stimulate the economy.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Result of pre-maturity bond purchase → Increased money supply and cheap currency
☛ Process of increasing money supply → Monetary expansion
☛ Effect of cheap currency → Lower interest rates and increased investment
☛ Cause of expensive currency → Central bank selling bonds
☛ Types of open market operations → Buying bonds (cheap currency) and selling bonds (expensive currency)
question_hi: यदि सरकार अपने बांड्स की ख़रीददारी उनकी परिपक्वता अवधि से पूर्व ही शुरू कर देती है (पूर्ण परिपक्व राशि पर), इस स्थिति में अर्थव्यवस्था में संचारित मुद्रा क्या कहलाएगी? (RPF SI 2018 (24/12/2018) Shift 1)
options_hi: हीटेड मुद्रा
सस्ती मुद्रा
सुलभ मुद्रा
महंगी मुद्रा
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सस्ती मुद्रा

Explanation:
जब सरकार अपने बांड्स को परिपक्वता से पहले खरीद लेती है, तो वह अर्थव्यवस्था में अतिरिक्त तरलता इंजेक्ट करती है। इससे मुद्रा की आपूर्ति बढ़ जाती है और ब्याज दरें गिर जाती हैं, जिससे मुद्रा सस्ती हो जाती है। इस प्रक्रिया को मौद्रिक प्रसार के रूप में जाना जाता है। सस्ती मुद्रा का अर्थ है कि उधार लेना आसान और सस्ता हो जाता है, जो निवेश और आर्थिक गतिविधियों को प्रोत्साहित करता है। इसके विपरीत, महंगी मुद्रा तब होती है जब केंद्रीय बैंक मुद्रा आपूर्ति को कम करने के लिए बांड बेचता है, जिससे ब्याज दरें बढ़ जाती हैं। यह क्रिया सरकार द्वारा अर्थव्यवस्था को प्रोत्साहित करने के लिए की जाती है।

question: What is one effect of liberalisation in the industrial sector? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Higher import taxes
Complete government control
Fewer job opportunities
Increased competition
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Increased competition

Explanation:
Liberalisation under the 1991 economic reforms removed the licence raj and government control from the industrial sector. This allowed private companies to establish industries without government permission. Entry of foreign investment and technology increased competition in the market. Sectors that were earlier government monopolies now have multiple players, leading to better quality and lower prices for consumers. Higher import taxes and complete government control are opposite to liberalisation, while job opportunities increased, not decreased.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Main objective of 1991 economic reforms → Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation
☛ System before liberalisation in industry → Licence Raj
☛ One effect of liberalisation → Increased competition
☛ Full form of FDI → Foreign Direct Investment
☛ Import tariffs under liberalisation → Reduced

question: Which type of unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between skills and job requirements? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Seasonal
Cyclical
Structural
Frictional
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Structural

Explanation:
Structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills of workers and the requirements of available jobs. This often results from technological changes, industry shifts, or globalization. For example, when a factory automates, demand for skilled machine operators falls while demand for programmers rises. This type of unemployment can be long-term and requires retraining or education to resolve. In contrast, seasonal unemployment happens at specific times of the year, cyclical unemployment is linked to the business cycle, and frictional unemployment occurs during the transition between jobs.

☛ Technological change leads to which type of unemployment → Structural
☛ When does frictional unemployment occur → During job transitions
☛ Cyclical unemployment is related to → Economic recession
☛ Example of seasonal unemployment → Agriculture and tourism

question: Which strategy, widely adopted in India's early economic planning, aimed to reduce foreign dependence and was a significant feature of industrial policy? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Globalisation
Export Promotion
Import Substitution
Liberalisation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Import Substitution

Explanation:
India's early economic planning (1950s) adopted the Import Substitution strategy to reduce foreign dependence by protecting domestic industries. It involved high tariffs, quotas, and licensing to limit imports. This was a key feature of the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, which gave the public sector a dominant role. The strategy aimed to develop self-reliance but led to a closed economy and inefficiency. Consequently, economic reforms in 1991 shifted towards liberalization and globalization. Import substitution was central to India's industrial policy until the balance of payments crisis prompted a change.

भारत की प्रारंभिक आर्थिक योजना (1950 के दशक) में आयात प्रतिस्थापन रणनीति अपनाई गई, जिसका उद्देश्य घरेलू उद्योगों को संरक्षण देकर विदेशी वस्तुओं पर निर्भरता कम करना था। इसके तहत उच्च टैरिफ और कोटा लगाए गए, और सरकार ने भारी उद्योगों को बढ़ावा दिया। यह औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प 1956 का प्रमुख हिस्सा था, जिसमें सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र को अग्रणी भूमिका दी गई। हालांकि, इस नीति के कारण अर्थव्यवस्था बंद हो गई और प्रतिस्पर्धा कम हुई, जिससे बाद में 1991 में आर्थिक सुधार लाए गए।

question: Which type of poverty is generally considered as a result of insufficient income? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Situational poverty
Absolute poverty
Relative poverty
Urban poverty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Absolute poverty

Explanation:
Absolute poverty refers to a condition where an individual's income is insufficient to meet basic survival needs such as food, clean water, healthcare, and shelter. It is often measured by a fixed income threshold. Situational poverty results from sudden crises, relative poverty denotes lack of resources compared to others in society, and urban poverty is a spatial phenomenon. Therefore, insufficient income directly leads to absolute poverty.

question: What is poverty? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Having a large population
Inability to fulfill basic needs like food, clothing and shelter
Lack of education
Lack of employment opportunities
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Inability to fulfill basic needs like food, clothing and shelter

Explanation:
Poverty is a state where an individual or community lacks the financial resources to meet basic necessities such as food, clothing, and shelter. It extends beyond low income to include limited access to healthcare, education, and social participation. The World Bank defines extreme poverty as living on less than $2.15 per day (2017 PPP). Poverty is multidimensional, encompassing deprivation in opportunities and social exclusion. It is often measured using the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), which considers factors like nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, and living standards.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the poverty line? → Minimum income level to meet basic needs
☛ International extreme poverty line? → $2.15 per day (2017 PPP)
☛ Who determines India's poverty line? → NITI Aayog
☛ Who releases the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)? → UNDP and OPHI
☛ Official methods for poverty estimation in India? → Tendulkar Committee (2009) and Rangarajan Committee (2014)

question: Which of the following directive principles of state policy is NOT provided by the Indian Constitution for its citizens? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Adequate means of livelihood
Ownership of the community material resources not distributed
Protection of children and youth against exploitation
Equal pay for equal work
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ownership of the community material resources not distributed

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51). These principles are non-justiciable but fundamental in governance. Among the given options, 'Ownership of the community material resources not distributed' is NOT a DPSP. Article 39(b) states that the ownership and control of community material resources shall be distributed so as to best serve the common good, not that they should not be distributed. The other options—Adequate means of livelihood (Article 39(a)), Protection of children and youth against exploitation (Article 39(e)), and Equal pay for equal work (Article 39(d))—are all part of DPSP.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What does Article 39(b) state? → Ownership and control of community material resources shall be distributed to best serve common good.
☛ Which Article deals with adequate means of livelihood? → Article 39(a).
☛ What does Article 39(d) provide? → Equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
☛ Which Article protects children and youth from exploitation? → Article 39(e).
☛ From which country are DPSP borrowed? → Ireland (Irish Constitution).

Solution: सही उत्तर है सामुदायिक भौतिक संसाधनों का स्वामित्व वितरित नहीं किया गया

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निदेशक सिद्धांत (DPSP) अनुच्छेद 36-51 में दिए गए हैं। ये सिद्धांत गैर-न्यायिक हैं लेकिन देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं। प्रश्न में दिए गए विकल्पों में से, 'सामुदायिक भौतिक संसाधनों का स्वामित्व वितरित नहीं किया गया' संविधान में DPSP के रूप में मौजूद नहीं है। अनुच्छेद 39(b) में कहा गया है कि सामुदायिक भौतिक संसाधनों का स्वामित्व और नियंत्रण इस प्रकार वितरित किया जाए कि सार्वजनिक भलाई के लिए सबसे अच्छा हो, न कि वितरित नहीं किया जाए। अन्य विकल्प जैसे जीविका के पर्याप्त साधन (अनुच्छेद 39(a)), शोषण से बच्चों और युवाओं की सुरक्षा (अनुच्छेद 39(e)), और समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन (अनुच्छेद 39(d)) DPSP का हिस्सा हैं।

question: Why is rural credit important for rural development in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: It reduces agricultural activities.
It supports urban migration.
It decreases industrial investment.
It helps farmers and small businesses access funds for production and development
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It helps farmers and small businesses access funds for production and development

Explanation:
Rural credit is crucial for rural development because it enables farmers and small businesses to access funds necessary for production and development. In India, agriculture plays a vital role in the economy, and most farmers are small and marginal, lacking adequate capital for investment. Through rural credit, they can purchase seeds, fertilizers, equipment, and other inputs, leading to increased productivity. Additionally, such credit helps in starting small industries and services in rural areas, generating employment opportunities and reducing poverty. Rural credit stimulates the rural economy, bridges the urban-rural divide, and contributes to overall development by ensuring that rural enterprises have the financial resources needed to grow and innovate.

☛ Central source of rural credit in India → NABARD
☛ Kisan Credit Card scheme → Launched to provide short-term loans to farmers
☛ Impact of rural credit → Increases agricultural productivity and reduces poverty
☛ Key institutions for rural credit → Cooperative banks, Regional Rural Banks, and Commercial Banks

Explanation:
ग्रामीण ऋण ग्रामीण विकास के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह किसानों और छोटे व्यवसायों को उत्पादन और विकास के लिए आवश्यक धन उपलब्ध कराता है। भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था में कृषि का महत्वपूर्ण स्थान है, और अधिकांश किसान छोटे एवं सीमांत हैं, जिनके पास निवेश के लिए पर्याप्त पूँजी नहीं होती। ग्रामीण ऋण के माध्यम से वे बीज, उर्वरक, उपकरण और अन्य इनपुट खरीद सकते हैं, जिससे उत्पादकता बढ़ती है। इसके अलावा, यह ऋण ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में लघु उद्योगों और सेवाओं को शुरू करने में मदद करता है, जिससे रोजगार के अवसर पैदा होते हैं और गरीबी कम होती है। ग्रामीण ऋण से ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को गति मिलती है, जो शहरी-ग्रामीण असमानता को कम करने और समग्र विकास में योगदान देती है।

question: The idea of human development is supported by the concepts of _____________________.1. Equity2. Sustainability3. Productivity4. Empowerment  (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2, 3 and 4
1, 2 and 3 only
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4

Explanation:
The idea of human development is supported by four core concepts: equity, sustainability, productivity, and empowerment. Equity means ensuring equal opportunities for all people. Sustainability implies that development does not compromise the ability of future generations. Productivity relates to the efficiency of people's capabilities and actions. Empowerment gives people the power to make decisions about their own lives. Together, these four pillars form the comprehensive concept of human development. Equity and empowerment are particularly emphasized in the capability approach by Amartya Sen, while sustainability and productivity ensure long-term economic and social progress. The Human Development Index (HDI) incorporates aspects of these concepts, but the broader idea includes all four.

☛ Which dimensions are included in the Human Development Index (HDI)? → Health, Education and Standard of Living
☛ What does equity in human development ensure? → Equal opportunities
☛ What is the meaning of sustainability in human development? → Long-term viability of development
☛ What is the main objective of empowerment in human development? → Giving people the power to make decisions

question: Which sector(s) in India has/have benefited maximum from globalisation? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: In 1971, the Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA) and Marginal Farmers and Agricultural Labourers (MFAL) Agency were introduced on the recommendations of the ___________ (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: What does LPG stand for in the context of India's economic reforms? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Low Price Goods
Labour Policy Guidelines
Liquefied Petroleum Gas
Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation

Explanation:
In the context of India's economic reforms initiated in 1991, LPG stands for Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation. Under these reforms, the government relaxed regulations (Liberalisation), transferred ownership of public sector enterprises to private hands (Privatisation), and opened up the economy to foreign trade and investment (Globalisation). This model helped India recover from a severe economic crisis and achieve higher growth rates. It is important to note that LPG in this context does not refer to Liquefied Petroleum Gas, a common confusion. The reforms were largely driven by then Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

question: Which of the following best describes seasonal unemployment? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Long-term unemployment
Unemployment during certain seasons of the year
Unemployment during economic downturns
Joblessness due to lack of skills
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Unemployment during certain seasons of the year

Explanation:
Seasonal unemployment refers to unemployment that occurs during specific seasons or periods of the year when the demand for labor in a particular industry or sector decreases. It is commonly observed in sectors like agriculture, tourism, and construction, which are dependent on weather or seasons. For instance, farmers become unemployed after harvest season. This differs from long-term unemployment, which is persistent, and from cyclical unemployment during economic downturns. To reduce seasonal unemployment, skill development and alternative employment opportunities are promoted. Hence, unemployment during certain seasons of the year best describes seasonal unemployment.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the main cause of seasonal unemployment? → Weather-dependent industries
☛ How is seasonal unemployment reduced in India? → Skill development and employment diversification
☛ What type of unemployment is seasonal unemployment? → Temporary unemployment
☛ How is MGNREGA related to seasonal unemployment? → It was designed to reduce seasonal unemployment
